If you are comparing late-winter versus early-spring timing, review our [Türkiye in winter travel guide](https://itineraryofturkiye.com/blog/turkey-in-winter-premium-travel-guide) alongside this March breakdown.
When does spring weather begin in Istanbul, Ephesus and Antalya?

Spring arrives from south to north during March. Official [MGM Antalya records](https://www.mgm.gov.tr/veridegerlendirme/il-ve-ilceler-istatistik.aspx?k=&m=ANTALYA) average 18.0°C highs and 6.7 daily sunshine hours, while [MGM Izmir data](https://www.mgm.gov.tr/veridegerlendirme/il-ve-ilceler-istatistik.aspx?k=&m=IZMIR) near Ephesus reaches 16.4°C highs. [MGM Istanbul normals](https://www.mgm.gov.tr/veridegerlendirme/il-ve-ilceler-istatistik.aspx?k=&m=ISTANBUL) stay cooler at 12.4°C highs and 5.5°C lows, warming noticeably after mid-month.

body.text: Archaeological sites such as the [Ephesus Archaeological Site](https://muze.gov.tr/Language/Index/EN?url=%2Fmuze-detay%3Fsectionid%3Defs01%26distid%3Defs), Hierapolis, and Perge remain on winter visiting hours until April 1, so start sightseeing by 09:00 to enjoy soft morning light before the 17:00–17:30 ticket cutoff.
Are coastal boutique hotels in Bodrum and Kaş open yet in March?

Only a select group of year-round hotels in Bodrum and Kaş operate in March, as most seasonal beach clubs and cliffside boutique properties open between mid-April and May 1. Town-center hotels in Bodrum Marina, Urla, Alaçatı, and Antalya Kaleiçi stay open all year, offering quiet waterfront stays at substantial shoulder-season discounts.

Before booking a coastal property in March, verify in writing whether its restaurant, spa, and heated pool are fully operational rather than in pre-season maintenance. Coastal road trips along the Lycian Way or Datça Peninsula are exceptionally calm in March, provided you treat them as scenic hiking and dining routes rather than beach-club holidays.
What changes around Nevruz (March 21) and early spring wildflowers?

Around Nevruz on March 21, lengthening daylight triggers wildflower blooms—anemones, wild orchids, and almond blossoms—across the Aegean hills, Lycian trails, and ancient marble ruins of Ephesus, Priene, and Olympos. Cultural celebrations mark the vernal equinox across Türkiye, and outdoor café terraces begin filling up on sunny afternoons in Izmir, Antalya, and Istanbul.

items: March 1–15: Best for lowest city hotel pricing, crisp Cappadocia mornings, and uncrowded indoor museums.
March 16–31: Warmer afternoons across the Aegean and Mediterranean, blooming orchards around Şirince and Urla, and improved daylight for Lycian Way day hikes.

Check annual holiday overlap: Because Ramadan and Eid al-Fitr (Ramazan Bayramı) shift earlier each year on the Gregorian calendar, confirm exact public-holiday dates before locking in domestic flights or museum days.

faq.q: Is March too cold to visit Istanbul?
faq.a: No. Istanbul averages 12.4°C highs in March with cool 5.5°C mornings—ideal for walking neighborhoods like Sultanahmet, Karaköy, and Kadıköy with a trench coat or light quilted jacket.

faq.q: Can you swim in Antalya or Bodrum in March?
faq.a: No, sea temperatures remain chilly in March, and most beach piers are not yet installed. Travelers visit the coast in March for hiking, archaeology, vineyards, and quiet harbor towns.

faq.q: Are Cappadocia valleys muddy in March?
faq.a: Yes, melting winter snow and spring showers can leave Cappadocia's volcanic clay trails slick, especially in early March. Waterproof hiking shoes with good grip are essential.

faq.q: Do museum summer hours start in March?
faq.a: No. State museums managed by the Ministry of Culture and Tourism switch from winter hours to extended summer hours on April 1, so March visits follow winter schedules.
